interactions.label: A clinician evaluating low back pain must first exclude specific causes before a

params.question: A clinician evaluating low back pain must first exclude specific causes before attributing it to a mechanical origin. Which of the following is NOT a specific cause of low back pain?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Ankylosing spondylitis is an inflammatory cause of LBP — one of the specific causes the clinician must exclude, particularly in young males with prolonged morning stiffness.
Correct. Facet joint arthropathy is a mechanical cause of LBP, part of the 85% that involves muscles, ligaments, and facet joints without nerve compression or structural pathology.
Incorrect. Pott's disease (tuberculous spondylitis) is an infective cause of LBP — a specific cause with an insidious course that must be actively excluded.
Incorrect. Spinal metastases are a neoplastic cause of LBP — one of the most important specific causes to rule out, especially in older patients with unexplained weight loss.

overallFeedback.feedback: Facet joint arthropathy is a mechanical cause (about 85% of LBP). The clinician's priority is to rule out specific causes: degenerative, inflammatory, infective, neoplastic, metabolic, and referred conditions.

Well done. The clinician must first exclude the 15% of specific causes — degenerative, inflammatory, infective, neoplastic, metabolic, and referred — before attributing back pain to a mechanical origin.

interactions.label: What is the primary initiating event in the degenerative cascade of the interver

params.question: What is the primary initiating event in the degenerative cascade of the intervertebral disc?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Facet hypertrophy is a secondary event — it occurs when the facets bear more load after the disc has already lost height.
Incorrect. Annular tears develop as a consequence of abnormal stress after the disc has already lost height and springiness.
Correct. Water content of the nucleus drops from about 80% in youth to 70% by the sixties, causing loss of disc height — this triggers the downstream cascade of annular tears and facet arthritis.
Incorrect. Nerve root compression is a late consequence of the degenerative process, occurring after disc height loss, annular tears, and foraminal narrowing.

overallFeedback.feedback: The cascade begins with desiccation of the nucleus pulposus. This loss of water content and disc height triggers annular tears and facet joint overloading — the two downstream chain reactions that narrow the space available for nerves.
Exactly right. Disc degeneration starts with desiccation of the nucleus pulposus, which triggers two chain reactions: annular tears from abnormal stress and facet joint arthritis from increased load.

interactions.label: A 50-year-old man has neck pain radiating to his left arm with biceps weakness a

params.question: A 50-year-old man has neck pain radiating to his left arm with biceps weakness and a depressed biceps reflex. Cervical X-rays show osteophytes and disc space narrowing at C5–C6. Why is an MRI still indicated despite these X-ray findings?

answers.text: X-rays cannot confirm the diagnosis of cervical spondylosis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. X-rays can show bony changes consistent with spondylosis. The limitation is that such changes are common even in people without symptoms.

answers.text: Degenerative X-ray changes are common in asymptomatic individuals and cannot confirm which level is causing the compression

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Degenerative changes appear commonly on X-rays after age 40 in asymptomatic people. MRI is needed to visualise the soft-tissue pathology and confirm that C5–C6 is truly the compressive level.

answers.text: X-rays cannot display osteophytes clearly enough for surgical planning

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. X-rays show osteophytes well. The limitation is that bony changes alone cannot demonstrate soft-tissue nerve root or cord compression.

answers.text: MRI is mandatory by protocol before any conservative treatment can begin

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. MRI is not required before starting conservative treatment. It is indicated when soft-tissue pathology needs to be visualised, particularly if surgery is being considered.

overallFeedback.feedback: Degenerative X-ray changes are common in asymptomatic individuals over 40. MRI shows soft-tissue pathology — disc, nerve roots, spinal cord — that X-rays cannot, and must be correlated with clinical findings to avoid treating the wrong level.

Spot on. Imaging without clinical correlation misleads — degenerative X-ray changes are present in many asymptomatic people over 40, so MRI is needed to confirm that the radiological level matches the clinical picture.

interactions.label: Strict bed rest is recommended as first-line conservative treatment for an acute

params.question: Strict bed rest is recommended as first-line conservative treatment for an acute prolapsed intervertebral disc.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Bed rest slows recovery rather than helping it. Conservative management includes anti-inflammatory medications, physiotherapy, and activity modification — keeping the spine moving — while the body gradually resorbs the herniated disc material.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Bed rest is actively discouraged because it slows recovery. Conservative management emphasises staying active with anti-inflammatory medications, physiotherapy, and activity modification while the herniated disc material is naturally resorbed.

params.question: A 58-year-old woman has bilateral leg pain on walking 300 metres that is relieved when she leans forward on a shopping trolley. Her pedal pulses are normal. Which feature most reliably distinguishes her condition from vascular claudication?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Both neurogenic and vascular claudication can present bilaterally. Distribution alone does not distinguish them.
Normal pulses make vascular disease unlikely, but the most reliable distinguishing feature is the pattern of symptom relief, not the pulse status alone.

answers.text: Relief with forward flexion rather than just standing still

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The hallmark of neurogenic claudication is positional relief — forward flexion opens the stenosed lumbar canal and decompresses the nerve roots. Vascular claudication improves with rest alone, regardless of posture.

answers.text: Onset of symptoms at a fixed walking distance

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Both conditions can present with a predictable claudication distance. This feature does not distinguish between them.

overallFeedback.feedback: Neurogenic claudication improves with forward flexion (the 'shopping-trolley sign') because flexion opens the narrowed lumbar canal. Vascular claudication improves simply by stopping, regardless of position. Normal pulses support the diagnosis but positional relief is the key differentiator.

Well done. The 'shopping-trolley sign' — relief with forward flexion — is the clinical hallmark of neurogenic claudication from lumbar spinal stenosis, distinguishing it from vascular claudication where rest alone relieves symptoms regardless of posture.
